source.title: HOW DO YOU ACCOUNT FOR YOUR INFORMATION?
source.intro: Gordon studies your request. “Before we discuss authorization: what are you prepared to put on the record about your source?”

choices.label: Keep the request focused on my findings. Do not identify a source.
reply: Your findings are yours to submit. I am not asking you to invent an authorization you do not possess.
Put the discrepancy through the proper channel. You are still not getting restricted records in this meeting.
choices.reflection: You did not identify Marge or show a restricted extract.

choices.label: Cite the authorized index reference Marge pointed me to.
reply: An index reference establishes which authorization you want checked. It does not grant access to the underlying operation.
You used the formal route. Keep using it.
choices.reflection: You relied on the official reference, not on a confidential disclosure.

choices.label: Name Marge as the person who confirmed your alias.
reply: Marge confirmed it? Then I will ask HR what was disclosed.
Do not confuse naming your source with verifying the insurance entry. Those remain different questions.
choices.reflection: You identified Marge after promising to protect her name. Gordon has said he will ask HR about the disclosure.

choices.label: Show the restricted administrative extract Marge supplied.
reply: That extract is restricted. Its circulation will need to be accounted for.
It identifies an administrative filing arrangement. It does not prove who typed the insurance entry, and it does not authorize you to inspect search records.
choices.reflection: You showed the restricted extract. You did not say Marge’s name, but its circulation may expose her help.

privacy.title: A FILE IS NOT AN INVITATION
privacy.intro: The folder contains routine office paperwork and a sealed personal letter marked PRIVATE. Nothing visible links the letter to John, the artifact or the insurance entry.
privacy.letter: Please do not sell the family house to cover the theatre’s debts. You have already paid more of its rent than anyone knows. I would rather close the place than let you lose everything keeping it open. And please stop telling me that a deficit is just a budget wearing a disguise.

choices.label: Leave the personal letter sealed.
choices.result: You leave the personal correspondence untouched. The routine paperwork establishes nothing about John.

choices.label: Read the private letter, but do not copy it.
choices.result: You read a family appeal about Gordon’s financial support for a theatre. It reveals vulnerability, not evidence about John. You do not make a copy.

choices.label: Read it and copy its wording into your private notes.
choices.result: You copy the personal letter. It is potentially useful pressure material, but it is not evidence in the investigation.
